newsitem.title: UK: P&I reinsurance rates set to tumble - industry.
newsitem.headline: P&I reinsurance rates set to tumble - industry.

text.p: The cost of reinsurance for shipowners' protection and indemnity (P&I) clubs is likely to fall by up to 40 percent next year, industry sources told Reuters.
"There will be big reductions, typically up to 40 percent," one senior industry source said.
P&I clubs are mutual organisations formed by shipowners to insure their vessels. Fourteen leading clubs form the s-called Group, which represents most of the sector.

P&I clubs in the Group paid approximately $250 million in reinsurance premiums for the 1996/97 year, but are in a strong position to press for a big reduction because of the low level of claims this year.
"There's a lot of detail still to be worked out, but underwriters understand that there is a case for a rate cut," said another P&I source, who forecast average rate reductions of 30 to 40 percent.

However, the structure of next year's P&I reinsurance programmes, which are due for renewal on February 20, was still being discussed and could lead to the clubs retaining more of the risk than in previous years.
A P&I clubs reinsurance sub-committee will meet on Monday, 16 December to discuss next year's renewal further.
"Brokers have probably got near to as good terms as they can get, but club managers are being leant on by various people, particularly by the ship-owners," one manager said.
The market for most types of reinsurance is currently soft due to a combination of surplus capacity and high profits after three years of low claims.
